name: Rogue RMM Tool Abuse
description: Threat actors increasingly deploy legitimate Remote Monitoring and Management (RMM) software â€” ScreenConnect, Atera, Action1, AnyDesk, Splashtop, PDQ, RustDesk, SimpleHelp, and Tactical RMM â€” as a 'living off the land' substitute for custom RATs, since signed RMM binaries rarely trigger AV/EDR alerts and blend into normal IT administration traffic. Huntress's 2026 Cyber Threat Report found a 277% year-over-year jump in RMM abuse alongside a 53% drop in traditional malware use, with over 50% of suspicious Atera activity directly tied to ransomware. Delivery is most often via phishing lures impersonating Microsoft Teams, Zoom, Excel, or Adobe installers (sometimes signed with stolen certificates), and frequently chains from the Teams-helpdesk-impersonation and ClickFix vectors. MuddyWater remains the canonical nation-state example of this technique, having weaponized Atera, ScreenConnect, PDQ, and Action1 across its 2025-2026 espionage campaigns, while criminal operators use multi-tool 'daisy-chains' (e.g., PDQ or GoTo Resolve dropping ScreenConnect, SimpleHelp, or MeshAgent) to establish redundant footholds before ransomware deployment.

mitre_techniques.notes: Core technique â€” legitimate RMM agents (ScreenConnect, Atera, Action1, AnyDesk, Splashtop, etc.) installed and used as the primary remote-access channel
RMM installers delivered disguised as Teams/Zoom/Excel/Adobe installers, sometimes signed with stolen certificates

mitre_techniques.technique_name: Masquerading: Match Legitimate Name or Location
mitre_techniques.notes: RMM binaries renamed or bundled to mimic trusted software, evading both user suspicion and signature-based controls
Once installed, RMM agents provide persistent external access points into the victim network
RMM tools provide GUI remote-desktop functionality used for hands-on-keyboard follow-on activity, including ransomware staging
RMM file-transfer features used to push secondary tools (credential dumpers, ransomware encryptors) to compromised hosts

notable_examples: Huntress 2026 Cyber Threat Report: 277% YoY increase in RMM abuse, 53% decline in traditional malware, with 50%+ of suspicious Atera activity linked to ransomware
February 2026: attackers used fake workplace-meeting lures with stolen digital certificates to silently deploy ScreenConnect, Tactical RMM, and MeshAgent in a layered chain

MuddyWater's August-October 2025 campaign against 100+ government/diplomatic targets relied on Atera Agent, ScreenConnect, PDQ Deploy/RMM, and Action1 for persistent access alongside the Phoenix v4 backdoor
Huntress SOC documented multi-tool 'daisy-chain' incidents where PDQ or GoTo Resolve is used to deploy secondary RMM tools (ScreenConnect, SimpleHelp) for redundancy
RustDesk and Atera abuse observed delivering ransomware in as little as 1-2 hours from initial RMM deployment to encryption
detection_opportunities: Inventory and allowlist approved RMM tools per environment; alert on installation of any RMM software not on the approved list
Alert on first-time-seen RMM agent installation/execution on a host with no prior history of that tool
Monitor for RMM installers delivered via email attachments or downloads disguised as Teams/Zoom/Excel/Adobe setup files, especially when signed with recently-issued or unusual certificates
Hunt for RMM tool installation immediately following a Teams/Quick Assist remote session or a ClickFix-style PowerShell execution
Flag chained RMM activity â€” one RMM tool (e.g., PDQ, GoTo Resolve) installing or launching a second RMM agent (ScreenConnect, SimpleHelp, MeshAgent)
Restrict outbound access to RMM vendor cloud relay domains/IPs at the network egress level for hosts that don't require them
Treat any unexpected RMM session immediately preceding credential dumping, lateral movement, or shadow-copy deletion as a high-confidence ransomware precursor
